findings.evidenceJa: 正体不明の黒い影
findings.governingReading: The enemy list includes a black shadow whose identity remains unknown.
findings.explanation: The English removes the explicit uncertainty about the shadow’s identity.

findings.evidenceJa: 臓硯の標的は桜だけだとしても
findings.governingReading: Even supposing Sakura alone is Zouken’s target, Shirou and Rin roaming town would be an obstruction.
findings.explanation: The English removes the conditional framing and asserts Sakura is his only target.

findings.highlight: we should get in his way if we’re walking about
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちが町を出歩けば目障りだろう
findings.governingReading: Shirou reasons that their visible movement through town would probably make them an eyesore or nuisance to Zouken.
findings.explanation: The English changes the predicted effect into an intention that they should interfere with him.

findings.highlight: a repeat of our encounter in the forest
findings.evidenceJa: あの森と同じ事が街中で起こる
findings.governingReading: At worst, the same kind of devastation that occurred in the forest could happen in the middle of town.
findings.explanation: The English narrows the feared urban disaster to repetition of the pair’s personal encounter.

findings.highlight: We don’t have anything to spare
findings.evidenceJa: お互い真剣に話し合う余裕なんてない
findings.governingReading: The situation affords neither of them the composure or time for a serious discussion.
findings.explanation: The English drops the act they lack room for and leaves a malformed generic statement.

findings.evidenceJa: その気持ちは嬉しいが、もう方針は決まっている。
findings.governingReading: Shirou appreciates Sakura’s concern, but the patrol policy has already been settled.
findings.explanation: A sentence-internal period leaves the English visibly malformed.

findings.highlight: If it bothers her that much, she shouldn’t have said it in the first place.
findings.evidenceJa: ばか
findings.governingReading: Shirou inwardly caps his recognition of Rin’s concealed concern by calling her an idiot.
findings.explanation: The English omits the affectionate exasperation that colors his reading of her denial.

findings.evidenceJa: 半端な態度をとったら
findings.governingReading: Rin says taking an ambiguous or half-hearted stance would give Zouken an opening.
findings.explanation: The English loses the specific danger of ambiguity and leaves the condition grammatically incomplete.

findings.highlight: what happened to her after she was adopted to the Matou family
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐に引き取られた事
findings.governingReading: Rin disclaims personal involvement in the fact that Sakura was taken in by the Matou family.
findings.explanation: The English changes the adoption into unspecified events after it and uses malformed “adopted to” phrasing.

findings.evidenceJa: 必死に騙そうとしてる
findings.governingReading: Shirou reads Rin’s clenched fist as proof she is desperately trying to deceive him and maintain the denial.
findings.explanation: The English changes interpersonal deception into an attempt to persuade herself.

findings.evidenceJa: 歯の浮くコト
findings.governingReading: Rin calls Shirou’s praise embarrassingly sentimental or teeth-settingly saccharine.
findings.explanation: The English changes emotional corniness into social arrogance.

findings.evidenceJa: ズカズカと歩き出す
findings.governingReading: Rin turns away and strides off heavily and forcefully.
findings.explanation: The English removes the physical force expressing her embarrassed retreat.

findings.highlight: you really can’t call it murder
findings.evidenceJa: 殺人って呼び方も怪しい
findings.governingReading: Rin says even calling the event murder is questionable because identities and missing body parts remain unclear.
findings.explanation: The English strengthens uncertainty about classification into inability to call it murder.

findings.highlight: You said this might be Zouken’s doing
findings.evidenceJa: これが臓硯の仕業じゃないって言った
findings.governingReading: Shirou reminds Rin that she said the incident was not Zouken’s doing and asks whether seeing the site changed her impression.
findings.explanation: The English reverses her earlier exclusion into the suggestion that Zouken might have caused it.

findings.highlight: leave the site of the tragedy
findings.evidenceJa: 荒れ地を後にする
findings.governingReading: They leave the wasteland-like ground where the tragedy likely occurred.
findings.explanation: The English removes the transformed physical character of the park.

findings.evidenceJa: これといった動きはなかった
findings.governingReading: There was no activity of particular note in Shinto.
findings.explanation: The English changes absence of notable events into the patrol party’s failure to find something.

findings.evidenceJa: 川べりからの冷たい風
findings.governingReading: They head home while receiving a cold wind from the riverside.
findings.explanation: The English removes the cold from the late-night atmosphere.

findings.evidenceJa: 帰路につく
findings.governingReading: Shirou and Rin set out on the way home.
findings.explanation: The English adds weary, heavy movement not stated in the source.

findings.highlight: she shouldn’t be able to use magic
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術は組み立てられない筈よ
findings.governingReading: Rin says Sakura should be unable to construct magecraft because no spare energy remains.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the technical act of constructing magecraft with generic use of magic.

findings.highlight: a bird that has a potential to fly
findings.evidenceJa: 鳥としてなら大空を飛べたモノ
findings.governingReading: The analogy begins with a creature that, as a bird, could have flown the open sky before being forced underwater.
findings.explanation: The English weakens counterfactual actual capability into potential and removes the open-sky contrast.

findings.evidenceJa: そう微笑む遠坂
findings.governingReading: Rin smiles so gently that Shirou’s heart skips.
findings.explanation: The English removes the visible smile and replaces it with an abstract trait.

findings.evidenceJa: 暇さえあれば見てた
findings.governingReading: Unable to speak much with Sakura, Rin watched her whenever she had the chance.
findings.explanation: The English removes the persistent frequency that reveals Rin’s sustained attention.

findings.highlight: I went to the archery club every day
findings.evidenceJa: 毎日のように弓道部に入り浸ってた
findings.governingReading: Rin practically haunted the archery club day after day after Sakura entered their school.
findings.explanation: The English converts near-daily frequency into an absolute daily claim.
